boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: Ten documented Pitt rituals, campus symbols, and game-day practices tied to the Pittsburgh campus.

cards.title: Pass the Light of Learning
cards.subtitle: Heinz Memorial Chapel and Cathedral of Learning
cards.notes: Look for the fall ceremony in which alumni illuminate first-year students’ commemorative lanterns, carrying the Light of Learning forward.
cards.short_summary: Pitt’s oldest tradition welcomes first-year students with illuminated lanterns.
cards.evidence_claim: Pitt identifies Lantern Night as its oldest tradition; alumni illuminate first-year students’ lanterns during the fall ceremony.
cards.access_notes: Attendance details vary by year; consult Pitt’s current Lantern Night information before planning.

cards.title: Read the Cathedral After a Win
cards.subtitle: Cathedral of Learning
cards.notes: After a Panthers victory or major University success, look to the Cathedral of Learning for its gold lighting and blue beam.
cards.short_summary: The Cathedral becomes a campus-scale signal of a Pitt win.
cards.evidence_claim: Pitt says the Cathedral is bathed in gold after football and other athletics wins, major University successes, and special events.
cards.source_title: Your handbook to the Pitt fandom
cards.access_notes: View from public outdoor areas around the Cathedral; lighting is tied to wins and designated occasions.

cards.title: Answer With Hail to Pitt
cards.subtitle: Pitt athletics and campus events
cards.notes: Learn the fight-song refrain and recognize H2P as the Pitt rallying phrase used across athletics and the wider University.
cards.short_summary: A fight song became Pitt’s shared shorthand and rallying cry.
cards.evidence_claim: Pitt traces Hail to Pitt and H2P to the University fight song and calls it a slogan and rallying cry for athletics and the University.
cards.source_title: Your handbook to the Pitt fandom
cards.access_notes: Listen at public Pitt events or use Pitt Band’s official lyrics resource linked by the University.

cards.title: Watch the Zoo’s First-Point Confetti
cards.subtitle: Petersen Events Center
cards.notes: At a Pitt basketball game, watch the Oakland Zoo’s first-point ritual: students toss discarded, ripped-up game papers as confetti.
cards.short_summary: Pitt basketball’s student section turns pregame papers into a first-basket shower.
cards.evidence_claim: Pitt reports that the Oakland Zoo distributes player-and-opponent papers and throws the torn papers when Pitt scores its first point.
cards.source_title: Your handbook to the Pitt fandom
cards.access_notes: Requires admission to the applicable basketball game; follow Petersen Events Center and event staff directions.

cards.title: Find the Panther Pitt End Zone
cards.subtitle: Acrisure Stadium, lower north end zone
cards.notes: At Pitt football games, identify the Panther Pitt student section across the lower north end zone and its coordinated T-shirts.
cards.short_summary: Pitt’s football student section occupies the lower north end zone.
cards.evidence_claim: Pitt identifies Panther Pitt as its football student section in Acrisure Stadium, spanning sections 116 through 127 in the lower north end zone.
cards.source_title: Your handbook to the Pitt fandom
cards.access_notes: Requires admission to a Pitt football game; student-section access and ticket rules are set by Pitt Athletics.

cards.title: Turn “So Good” Into “Go Pitt!”
cards.subtitle: Acrisure Stadium, end of the third quarter
cards.notes: During the third-quarter break, listen for Pitt fans linking arms and adding Pitt-specific calls to the stadium’s Sweet Caroline singalong.
cards.short_summary: A 2008 football-game singalong has Pitt-specific call-and-response lines.
cards.evidence_claim: Pitt says fans stand and link arms at the end of the third quarter, singing Sweet Caroline with “Go Pitt!” and “Let’s Go Pitt!” substitutions; the practice began in 2008.
cards.source_title: Your handbook to the Pitt fandom
cards.access_notes: Occurs during Pitt home football games; a game ticket is required for stadium access.

cards.entity_name: Pitt Homecoming Laser and Fireworks Show
cards.title: See the Homecoming Cathedral Show
cards.subtitle: Cathedral of Learning and Bigelow Boulevard
cards.notes: During Homecoming programming, watch for the longtime Friday-night display that combines synchronized music, lasers, fireworks, and the Cathedral.
cards.short_summary: Pitt Homecoming has used a Cathedral-focused laser and fireworks show since 1990.
cards.evidence_claim: The Pitt News reports that Pitt’s Homecoming week has included a Friday-night laser and fireworks show since 1990.
cards.source_title: Behind the scenes: PPC’s explosive homecoming tradition
cards.access_notes: Programming and viewing arrangements can change annually; use current Pitt Homecoming announcements.

cards.title: Spot the Shined-Up Panther Nose
cards.subtitle: Millennium Panther, Pittsburgh campus
cards.notes: Find the Millennium Panther and notice its well-known nose-rubbing custom, documented as a good-luck practice for exams and football games.
cards.short_summary: A 2001 Panther sculpture became the focus of Pitt good-luck lore.
cards.evidence_claim: The Pitt News reports that students began rubbing the Millennium Panther’s nose for luck on exams, and later for football games.
cards.access_notes: View the sculpture respectfully; do not climb on or damage campus artwork.

cards.title: Step Across Forbes Field’s Home Plate
cards.subtitle: Posvar Hall, first floor
cards.notes: In Posvar Hall, locate the embedded former Forbes Field home plate and follow the documented good-luck custom of stepping across it.
cards.short_summary: A preserved baseball home plate anchors a small Pitt good-luck ritual indoors.
cards.evidence_claim: The Pitt News states that Forbes Field’s former home plate is embedded in Posvar Hall and describes stepping on or sliding across it as a good-luck practice.
cards.access_notes: Use normal pedestrian access and avoid obstructing hallways or nearby offices.

cards.entity_name: Nationality and Heritage Rooms Holiday Open House
cards.title: Enter the Holiday Open House
cards.subtitle: Cathedral of Learning Commons and Nationality and Heritage Rooms
cards.notes: During the annual open house, explore decorated rooms and join the cultural demonstrations and traditional crafts presented by room committees.
cards.short_summary: The Nationality Rooms’ annual open house brings winter traditions into the Cathedral.
cards.evidence_claim: Pitt’s 2025 Holiday Open House invited guests to decorated Nationality and Heritage Rooms for crafts and cultural demonstrations, and described the event as free and open to the public.
cards.access_notes: The cited 2025 event was free and open to the public; confirm the current year’s date and access details before visiting.
